title: Revelation Control
abstract: arXiv:2608.23860v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Revelation Control is the problem of choosing priced interventions that reveal hidden state only insofar as the revealed distinctions can change a consequential decision, while accounting separately for any useful progress created by the intervention itself. We develop this theory for learning systems, where states equivalent under declared current information can respond differently to future training and favor different actions. The framework defines decision-sufficient revelation and revelation depth, separates pure information value from productive reuse, embeds static Bayes refinement into state-dependent continuation value, and gives an exact cost-adjusted factorization criterion: an additional shallow coordinate is decision-nonredundant only when states sharing a scalar summary lie on opposite sides of the priced Stop/Continue boundary. tldr: 本文提出了“揭示控制”理论，通过定价干预仅揭示能改变决策的隐藏状态，并引入决策充分性和成本调整因子化准则，以优化学习系统中的信息价值与生产性重用。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "Revelation Control" theory, which prices interventions to reveal hidden state only when it changes consequential decisions, and proposes decision-sufficiency and a cost-adjusted factorization criterion to optimize information value and productive reuse in learning systems.
